rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow Roberts opinion rejecting the Eighth Circuit’s categorical “bad faith or gross misjudgment” requirement and reaffirming that compensatory damages under Title II/§504 follow the familiar intentional-discrimination/deliberate-indifference framework. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas or Alito in dissent (warning about IDEA overlap and pedagogical deference), and from one or more majority justices to emphasize limiting principles (exhaustion, causation, and meaningful-access/reasonable-accommodation constraints).
